title: Divisional charts (vargas) explained for beginners | Ask Tota
description: Divisional charts split each sign into smaller parts to zoom in on one area of life. Parashara's 16 vargas, what each shows, and how much birth time each needs.
og_title: Divisional charts, the zoom lenses of a kundli
og_description: D9 for marriage, D10 for career, D60 for everything. The sixteen vargas, what each one shows, and why some need a birth time accurate to two minutes.
h1: divisional charts are the zoom lenses on ur kundli
dek: ur main chart is the wide shot. divisional charts, called vargas, cut each sign into smaller slices and redraw the whole chart from them, one for marriage, one for career, one for parents. parashara lists sixteen. here is what each is for, and how much birth time precision it demands.

llms_desc: what divisional charts (vargas) are in Vedic astrology, the sixteen shodashavarga charts from Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra and what each signifies (D1, D2, D3, D4, D7, D9, D10, D12, D16, D20, D24, D27, D30, D40, D45, D60), how they are calculated, and how birth time accuracy limits them.

faq.q: what are divisional charts in vedic astrology?
faq.a: charts made by dividing each 30 degree sign into equal parts and mapping each part to a sign. every planet's position in those small parts is redrawn as a new chart. each divisional chart is used to look closely at one area of life.

faq.q: how many divisional charts are there?
faq.a: brihat parashara hora shastra describes sixteen, called the shodashavarga: d1, d2, d3, d4, d7, d9, d10, d12, d16, d20, d24, d27, d30, d40, d45 and d60. some traditions use additional ones.

faq.q: which divisional chart is most important?
faq.a: after the d1 birth chart, the d9 navamsa is treated as the most important. it is used for marriage and for judging the real strength of every planet. the d10 for career is the next most consulted.
the navamsa shows marriage and the spouse, dharma, and the inner strength of planets. a planet strong in d1 but weak in d9 is read as promising more than it delivers.
the dashamsa shows career, profession, status and achievements in public life. it is read alongside the 10th house of the main chart.

the shashtiamsa is linked to past life karma and parashara gives it the highest weight among the vargas. it changes about every two minutes of birth time, so it is only usable with a very precise birth time.

faq.q: how accurate does my birth time need to be for divisional charts?
faq.a: it depends on the chart. the d9 lagna changes roughly every 13 minutes on average, the d10 every 12, and the d60 every 2. if ur birth time is rounded to the nearest half hour, trust the d1 and use the finer vargas carefully.
a planet occupying the same sign in the d1 and the d9. it is traditionally read as a sign of strength and consistency.

faq.q: what is d7 chart used for?
faq.a: the saptamsa is used for children and progeny, and more broadly for creative output and legacy.
the trimshamsa, used to examine misfortunes, health vulnerabilities and character flaws. unlike most vargas, its divisions are unequal, ruled by mars, saturn, jupiter, mercury and venus.

faq.q: do i need divisional charts as a beginner?
faq.a: start with the d1 and the d9. the d1 shows the whole picture and the d9 checks it. add the d10 if career is the question. the higher vargas are specialist tools.

faq.q: can divisional charts contradict the main chart?
faq.a: they refine it rather than overrule it. the classical rule is that a varga can modify what the d1 promises, but cannot create something the d1 does not show at all.
